analysis:
Examined docs/provider/troubleshooting.md (base and head), the new UnauthorizedConnectionRecovery.swift (patch and head text), and the metadata for ServingReadiness.swift. The docs change adds a `coordinator traffic` doctor row and expands the 'heartbeats arrive but requests do not' row. UnauthorizedConnectionRecovery is a pure decision helper: it re-registers a connection the coordinator has not authorized, after 15 min plus per-process jitter, then backs off 30 min, 1 h, 2 h and 4 h, and only when idle (`busy` false).

Security view: the helper grants no authorization and sends no data. Re-registration goes through the existing TB-002 and TB-011 registration, so the coordinator re-verifies attestation and App Attest and issues a fresh grant. This does not touch T-052 (authorization derived from labels) or T-053 (stale authorization surviving a connection change). A new socket means a new nonce and a new authorization decision, so a stale grant is not reused. The retry cadence is bounded (4 h cap, jitter) and gated on idleness, so it adds little load to the coordinator and no DoS vector (T-057). `connectionLacksAuthorization` fails toward 'lacks authorization' for untrusted, offline or no-status, and treats a status with no authorization object as not judged. Because it only triggers reconnects, that is not a security bypass.

One documented behavior to confirm in integration: the helper exempts `path == "legacy"` from the lack-of-authorization check. This only suppresses reconnects and does not grant anything.

The ServingReadiness.swift source text (178 lines) was not supplied, only its metadata and a truncated patch excerpt, so I could not review its verdict logic. Diagnostic output could in theory echo coordinator-supplied reasons (T-058, T-056 overclaim). The wiring into ProviderLoop+ServingAuthorizationRecovery.swift, and whether `busy` covers in-flight requests and the add-on hold (TB-012, A-018), are also outside the supplied evidence. Both should be checked in the next pass; neither is a supported finding.
